spec_match.rationale: Concepts map the exact current CSS Color 5 grammar — alpha() = alpha( [from <color>] [ / [<alpha-value> | none] ]? ), with the alpha component keyword referencing the origin's alpha (1.0 ≡ 100%) and the result staying in the origin's color space — through replace (/ 80%) and scale (calc(alpha * k)) forms, with rgb(from …) relative-color syntax kept distinct as a current baseline, not called legacy or deprecated. Syntax and current computed contracts are checked via CSS.supports plus getComputedStyle(), never authored-text echo. Parent review also records that current WPT explicitly flags unresolved/inconsistent alpha() resolution and serialization cases (CSSWG issues #13992/#13994), so accepted notation is not overstated as settled semantics. Layers kept separate: syntax, receiver, alpha keyword semantics, percentages/numbers, calc/channel math, color-space preservation, computed serialization, and fallback.

interactive.rationale: Real controls drive real painting: origin color/alpha pickers with replace-vs-scale modes (alpha-lab), side-by-side alpha()-vs-rgb(from) computed comparison (space-preserved), and a live brand-token re-tint across scrim/tint/ring/disabled surfaces (translucent-tokens). Fallbacks are labelled, never faked.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index and ledes match delivered concepts and the current spec. Fixed three bare 'ships in Chrome 152' fallback claims (alpha-lab, space-preserved, translucent-tokens) to provenanced availability: v152 listing Enabled by default; detail desktop 152 'Proposed' (updated 2026-07-17); the draft marks Relative Alpha Colors 'at-risk'; ChromeStatus records Firefox as Shipped/Shipping. Index renamed 'why it exists' and now notes the v150 sibling route for the same feature (both identities live, no merging).

edge_cases.rationale: Fallback honesty is structural: pages detect via CSS.supports and label which engine painted each swatch (native alpha(), rgb(from…) fallback, or sRGB fallback), and space-preserved now distinguishes computed coordinate-space evidence from visible gamut mapping: unequal serialized strings do not by themselves prove clipping or a visible pixel difference, and output depends on the display. The draft's at-risk marking and the Editor's-Draft mutability are surfaced, not hidden.

references.rationale: All four pages cite ChromeStatus and CSS Color 5 #relative-alpha; only the family index additionally cites CSS Color 4 #transparency for <alpha-value>. The current WPT files are linked from the draft; the spec lists live WPT (alpha-color-computed/parsing-valid/parsing-invalid), recorded as spec-referenced test coverage.

conformance.rationale: New immutable root suite (8 JSON entries = 8 rendered rows = 8 reported) now contains target contracts only: numeric and percentage parsing, omitted-alpha computation, none computation, calc(alpha) parsing, replace computation, scaled-origin-alpha computation, and display-p3 space preservation. Parent removed generic CSS namespace/static checks and rgb(from) baseline padding. Chrome 150 renders 0 pass / 8 fail / 0 blocked honestly; direct target behavior is absent.

runtime_evidence.rationale: chrome-devtools-mcp on HeadlessChrome/150 (2026-07-25): all visible controls exercised at 1280×800 and 390×844 with post-interaction geometry — alpha-lab support probe and replace/scale swatches with computed read-backs and labelled fallbacks, space-preserved two-column comparison with unavailable-left honesty, tokens brand re-tint across all four surfaces. Parent review corrected the space demo so computed serialization proves coordinate space but not visible clipping, and fixed alpha-lab telemetry to accept modern color-space serialization; zero console errors and zero failed requests.

telemetry_health.rationale: Concepts emit showcaseTelemetry.assert events per branch (alpha-native-paint/fallback-labelled, space-both-evaluated/unsupported-labelled, and tokens-alpha-derived/fallback-labelled with computed or painted values); telemetry POSTs returned 202 during validation.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, button background+color pairs, focus-visible styles, checkerboard/swatch regions labelled, no static-card pattern; edits were copy-level and preserve layout.

accessibility.rationale: role=status/aria-live on support lines and read-backs, mode buttons use aria-pressed, form controls are labelled, and computed values are exposed as text (not color-only).

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Matrix pass including post-interaction states: all four pages scrollWidth equals viewport at 1280×800 and 390×844 after every control (mode switches, slider changes, brand re-tint).

openQuestions.title: Verify native alpha() painting and at-risk fate on a Chrome 152+ build
openQuestions.detail: This build (HeadlessChrome/150) lacks alpha() (CSS.supports false for both forms; rgb(from …) relative-color syntax works and is used by labelled fallbacks). On a Chrome 152+ build (v152 listing Enabled by default; detail desktop 152 'Proposed' updated 2026-07-17), verify all 8 direct suite contracts, including omitted-alpha and none computation, numeric/percentage parsing, alpha(from #ff0000 / 50%) semantics, calc-scaled 0.4 alpha, and display-p3 origin-space preservation. Reconcile results with the current WPT warning that alpha() resolution/serialization expectations remain inconsistent (CSSWG #13992/#13994); compare semantic channels/space rather than requiring one unsettled notation. The draft marks Relative Alpha Colors at-risk and the Editor's Draft is mutable — recheck the section's existence and grammar before citing it again.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible live region announcements for dynamic probe/status results after button activation
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce dynamic state through live regions tied to the activating control; expose state in text, not color-only.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Verified applied: support lines and computed read-backs use role=status/aria-live; every painted result is also serialized as text (for example rgba() or color()) so the outcome is readable without color perception.

guidanceConsulted.query: swatch and card grids that stay contained on narrow mobile after live style updates
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Re-measure geometry after dynamic style/content changes, not only on initial load; wrap long declarations.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied per the standing lesson: post-interaction document width re-measured after mode switches and brand changes on all four pages.

summary: Source-review of the Relative Alpha Colors family against the current CSS Color 5 draft (alpha() = alpha( [from <color>] [ / [<alpha-value> | none] ]? ); alpha keyword ≡ origin's alpha, 1.0 = 100%; result in the origin's color space; section marked at-risk), the direct chromestatus detail (updated 2026-07-17: v152 listing Enabled by default; detail desktop 152 'Proposed'; ff=1 Shipped/Shipping, safari=5 No signal, and webdev=4 No signals per core_enums), and CSS Color 4 §4.2 for the alpha-value baseline. The family used CSS.supports, computed read-backs, and labelled fallbacks, but parent review corrected claims that string inequality proved clipping/visible gamut loss, removed 'legacy' terminology for current rgb(from …) syntax, and fixed native telemetry that only accepted rgb()/rgba() serialization. Hardened: three bare 'ships in Chrome 152' fallback claims are now provenanced (listing vs 'Proposed' detail vs at-risk draft vs ChromeStatus's Firefox Shipped/Shipping value), the index is 'why it exists' with the at-risk/mutability and v150-sibling identity notes. Added the immutable root suite; parent replaced five prerequisite/baseline rows with direct alpha() number, percentage, omitted, none, calc, computed-channel, and display-p3-space contracts (0/8 pass here, honestly). Missing-suite denominator 4→3 expected (795/798).
